briefings.title: Essential Truths w/ Howard Marks, Nima Shayegh & William Green (RWH066)
briefings.tldr: Successful investing and living require a radical commitment to humility, distinguishing between what can and cannot be controlled, and focusing on the qualitative "roots" of value rather than the quantitative "branches" of market noise.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** Successful investing and living require a radical commitment to humility, distinguishing between what can and cannot be controlled, and focusing on the qualitative "roots" of value rather than the quantitative "branches" of market noise.

## Navigating Technological Euphoria and AI
Howard Marks (Co-founder, Oaktree Capital Management) provides a framework for evaluating the current AI boom by drawing parallels to historical market cycles.

* **The Productivity vs. Profitability Gap:** While AI will undoubtedly change the world and increase productivity, it is not guaranteed to produce investor profits.
    * **Historical Context:** Like the internet bubble of 1999, the technology may be revolutionary, but the benefits often accrue to the consumer via lower prices or are eroded by competition.
* **Avoidable Mistakes in Euphoric Markets:**
    * **The "Lottery Ticket" Mentality:** Investing in low-probability laggards because they are "cheap" relative to leaders.
    * **Permanence Bias:** Assuming today’s tech leaders will inherently remain tomorrow’s leaders.
* **Risk Posture:** Investors must choose their game plan: making "binary bets" on novel startups (moonshots) versus investing in established companies where AI is incremental.

## The "I Don't Know" School: Uncertainty and Survival
Howard Marks emphasizes that market survival is predicated on respecting the unpredictability of the future.

* **Probability Distributions:** Marks views the future not as a fixed outcome, but as a range of possibilities. Only one thing will happen, but many things *can* happen.
* **Humility as a Tool:** Admitting "I don’t know" prevents investors from betting the house on a single certain outcome. 
    * **Knowing Limitations:** Marks quotes *Dirty Harry*: "A man’s got to know his limitations." Success comes from staying within one's "circle of competence" rather than trying to be extraordinary.
* **The "Gravy Train" Strategy:**
    * **Focus on Compounding:** Wealth is built by getting on the "gravy train" of economic growth and company productivity early and refusing to "tamper" with it.
    * **Defensive Mindset:** In uncertain times, it is better to avoid losers than to desperately hunt for winners.

## Investing in "Roots": Qualitative vs. Quantitative
Nima Shayegh (Founder, Rumi Partners) argues that the investment industry is overly focused on "branches" (quantifiable data) while ignoring "roots" (the causal forces behind the data).

* **Branches vs. Roots Framework:**
    * **Branches:** Metrics everyone can see—last quarter’s margins, unit growth, or inflation prints. These are often devoid of context.
    * **Roots:** Qualitative forces like management motivation, corporate culture, and customer alignment. These "live upstream" from the financials and dictate future economics.
* **"Eye of the Heart" (Cheshm-e-del):** Shayegh references a Persian concept suggesting that the heart is a faculty of perception capable of grasping non-material truths like sincerity and beauty.
* **"Blown-away-ness":** This is a physiological indicator of quality. Shayegh uses the example of Tesla’s Full Self-Driving or the first time using an iPhone—experiences so superior they create a sense of awe that cannot be captured in a spreadsheet.

## Lessons from the Greats: Lou Simpson and Simplicity
Shayegh reflects on his mentorship under Lou Simpson (former Geico investment chief), highlighting the temperament required for world-class compounding.

* **Temperament over Tools:** Simpson’s office lacked Bloomberg terminals and financial TV; it functioned like a library. He prioritized "thinking more and acting less."
* **The Danger of Hyperactivity:** Constantly reacting to data points destroys mental health and eventually degrades decision-making quality. 
* **Radical Humility:** Despite his legendary status, Simpson was quick to say "I don't know" and remained open to dissenting views, which gave him a clearer perception of reality.

## Personal Resilience and Stoic Philosophy
Host William Green discusses applying Stoic principles to handle the inherent suffering and setbacks of both markets and life.

* **Control and Reaction:** Drawing on Epictetus, Green notes that we cannot control external events (market crashes, health issues), only our internal reactions to them.
* **Enacting the "Given Part":** Life casts individuals in various roles—some as rulers, some as "cripples" or "poor men." The duty is not to choose the role, but to "enact well the given part."
* **The Stockdale Paradox:** Highlighting James Stockdale’s survival in a Vietnam POW camp, Green emphasizes that one must never do anything shameful that would "corrode the will" or offend one's own conscience.

***

> "The cautious seldom err or write great poetry. Every person has to decide for themselves: do I want to try to write great poetry and get rich if my bets are right, or do I want to avoid erring and be sure that I'll do okay if my bets are wrong?" 
> — **Howard Marks**

> "Maybe you're searching among the branches for what only appears in the roots." 
> — **Nima Shayegh** (quoting Rumi)

> "Remember, you are an actor in a drama of such sort as the author chooses... see that you enact it well, for this is your business: to enact well the given part." 
> — **William Green** (referencing Epictetus)

briefings.title: LIVE:  U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent Speaks at Economic Club of Dallas | AF15
briefings.tldr: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent outlined an "America First" economic strategy centered on three pillars—industrial dominance, domestic investment, and preparedness—to ensure economic sovereignty while introducing "Trump Accounts" to broaden citizen participation in the U.S. equity market.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent outlined an "America First" economic strategy centered on three pillars—industrial dominance, domestic investment, and preparedness—to ensure economic sovereignty while introducing "Trump Accounts" to broaden citizen participation in the U.S. equity market.

## The Three Pillars of Economic Security
*   **Industrial and Technological Dominance:** The administration is prioritizing the reshoring of critical industries to eliminate "single points of failure" exposed by the COVID-19 pandemic and the "China shock."
    *   **AI Infrastructure:** Bessent describes AI and quantum computing as existential battlegrounds for national security, noting that Treasury is working via the Financial Stability Oversight Council to promote responsible AI adoption in finance.
    *   **Digital Assets:** The administration supports a dollar-based stablecoin market to reinforce the U.S. dollar’s global role, supported by oversight tools provided by the GENIUS Act.
*   **Investment in America:** Maintaining the liquidity and credibility of the U.S. Treasury market is viewed as the foundation of global finance.
    *   **Strategic Capital:** Treasury intends to evaluate supervisory frameworks over the next six months to better mobilize capital toward semiconductors, energy infrastructure, and defense innovation.
*   **Preparedness and Deterrence:** Economic security requires proactive measures to prevent geopolitical shocks from causing domestic instability.
    *   **Supply Chain Vulnerability:** Bessent highlighted that 90% of advanced chips are still manufactured in Taiwan, representing a significant risk frontier alongside potential cyberattacks on financial infrastructure.

## Financial Inclusion via "Trump Accounts"
*   **Direct Seed Investment:** To address the fact that 40% of Americans have no equity market exposure, the administration is launching "Trump Accounts"—a $1,000 Treasury-funded seed investment for every eligible American child at birth.
*   **Philanthropic Support:** Texas natives Michael and Susan Dell have committed a $6.25 billion donation to "top up" these accounts for 25 million children in lower-income zip codes.
*   **Long-term Growth:** The funds are invested in a diversified index tied to the U.S. economy and remain locked for 18 years, though they can be rolled into retirement accounts or used for business startups and home down payments.
*   **Legislative Roots:** Bessent credited Texas Senator Ted Cruz with authoring the precursor to this provision.

## Banking Reform and Private Credit
*   **Small and Community Banks:** Bessent aims to address the "too small to succeed" trend by supporting legislation for enhanced non-interest-bearing accounts with deposit insurance up to $10 million to help local banks retain payroll and business clients.
*   **Private Credit Oversight:** While acknowledging that private credit provided a necessary "bridge" during tight regulatory periods, Treasury is focused on preventing "contagion" between unregulated capital and the regulated banking system.
*   **Retail Protection:** The administration is committed to ensuring that 401(k) plans do not become a "dumping ground" for bad assets from private equity "continuation funds."

## Tariff Strategy and Judicial Rulings
*   **Supreme Court Response:** Regarding the recent 6-3 Supreme Court ruling on IEEPA (International Emergency Economic Powers Act) authorities, Bessent clarified that while the court limited revenue collection under IEEPA, it did not strike down the tariffs themselves.
*   **Alternative Authorities:** The administration will pivot to using Section 232 (national security), Section 301 (unfair trade practices), and Section 122 (global tariffs) to maintain revenue levels.
*   **Revenue Outlook:** Treasury estimates that total tariff revenue for 2026 will remain virtually unchanged despite the shift in legal authorities.

## National Debt and Macro Outlook
*   **Deficit Reduction:** Bessent set a target to reduce the deficit-to-GDP ratio from the current ~7% down to 3% by the end of the President’s term through a combination of spending restraint and economic growth.
*   **Labor Market and AI:** Bessent expressed optimism regarding the labor market, citing a 12-14% CAPEX boom forecast for 2025. He views AI more as a tool for labor reallocation than pure displacement.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "A nation that cannot produce the critical goods and resources to sustain itself is exposed and vulnerable to coercion." — **Scott Bessent**

> "Movement of capital... capital goes where it's treated the best. I think it'd be good for Dallas and Texas just to take in productive private capital rather than government agencies." — **Scott Bessent**

> "Despite the misplaced gloating from Democrats... the court did not rule against President Trump's tariffs. Six justices simply ruled that IEEPA authorities cannot be used to raise even one dollar of revenue. This administration will invoke alternative legal authorities." — **Scott Bessent**

> "Economic security, above all else, is the foundation of sovereignty and thus the grantor of prosperity." — **Scott Bessent**

briefings.title: LIVE: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent Speaks At Economic Club Of Dallas Amid Tariff Ruling | WION
briefings.tldr: Scott Bessent, a key economic advisor and potential Treasury Secretary, outlines a "security-first" economic framework for a second Trump term centered on industrial dominance, a 3% deficit-to-GDP target, and a proposal for universal seed investment accounts for American children.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Scott Bessent, a key economic advisor and potential Treasury Secretary, outlines a "security-first" economic framework for a second Trump term centered on industrial dominance, a 3% deficit-to-GDP target, and a proposal for universal seed investment accounts for American children.

## The Shift Toward Industrial and Technological Dominance
* **Addressing the "China Shock":** Bessent argues that previous administrations prioritized short-term efficiency and corporate profit over national security, leading to a hollowed-out industrial base and a vulnerable supply chain.
* **Technological Supremacy:** The strategy focuses on maintaining a global edge in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and advanced manufacturing to ensure resilience against foreign suppliers.
* **The Dollar as a Strategic Asset:** Maintaining the U.S. dollar’s status as the global reserve currency is viewed as a critical component of national dominance.

## "Investment in America" and the "Trump Accounts"
* **Treasury Market Liquidity:** Economic security is tied directly to a strong and liquid U.S. Treasury market; Bessent warns this stability cannot be taken for granted.
* **Universal Seed Investments:** A proposal for "Trump Accounts" would provide a $1,000 seed investment for every eligible American child at birth.
    * **Objectives:** These funds would be placed in a diversified index tied to long-term U.S. growth to promote financial literacy and give all citizens a "stake" in the economy.
    * **Fiscal Concerns:** Critics and analysts note that the funding source for these accounts must be weighed against its impact on total government debt and spending.

## Fiscal Policy and Debt Management
* **Deficit Reduction Targets:** Bessent aims to reduce the deficit-to-GDP ratio to 3% by the conclusion of a potential second Trump term. 
* **The "Growth Path" Out of Debt:** In response to whether the U.S. faces growth, austerity, or inflation, Bessent asserts that the administration would choose a combination of robust economic growth and spending restraint.
* **Inflation Stance:** Bessent explicitly stated that high inflation is "not an option," signaling a preference for policies that protect purchasing power, though this may conflict with high-spending initiatives.

## Implications for Precious Metals and Global Markets
* **Bullish Case for Gold/Silver:** If the administration’s spending initiatives (like the "Trump Accounts") lead to increased government debt and downward pressure on the dollar, it would create a favorable environment for gold and silver.
* **Bearish Case for Gold/Silver:** If the administration successfully implements deficit reduction and maintains a strong dollar, it will likely act as a headwind for precious metals.
* **Market Monitoring:** The key indicator for investors will be the successful implementation of the 3% deficit target versus the actual scale of new spending programs.

> "He aims to bring the deficit-to-GDP ratio down to 3% by the time Trump would leave office." — Scott Bessent

> "Inflation is 'not an option' for the American people." — Scott Bessent

> "Previous administrations prioritized efficiency and profit over security and resilience, which led to a hollowed-out industrial base and a dangerous reliance on foreign suppliers for critical goods." — Scott Bessent (paraphrased from speech)

briefings.title: Secretary Hegseth remarks to the Rakkasans of the 101st Airborne at Fort Campbell.
briefings.tldr: Secretary Hegseth outlines a "back to basics" doctrine for the Department of War, prioritizing the restoration of the "warrior ethos" by eliminating social engineering, increasing defense spending, and "unleashing" warfighters through the removal of restrictive rules of engagement.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Secretary Hegseth outlines a "back to basics" doctrine for the Department of War, prioritizing the restoration of the "warrior ethos" by eliminating social engineering, increasing defense spending, and "unleashing" warfighters through the removal of restrictive rules of engagement.

## Cultural Shift: Restoring the Warrior Ethos
*   **Elimination of Distractions:** Hegseth asserts that previous administrations introduced "distractions" like Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI), social justice, and social engineering that do not belong in a "foxhole."
*   **Unity Over Diversity:** He explicitly rejects the phrase "our diversity is our strength," arguing instead that **unity of purpose and cohesion** are what make a unit strong.
*   **Merit and Lethality:** The department is pivoting back to core fundamentals: accountability, lethality, warfighting, readiness, training, and discipline.
*   **Personal Connection:** Hegseth highlighted his own history as a Rakkasan (101st Airborne) in Samarra, Iraq (2005-2006), noting that the unit’s identity is built on training hard and maintaining a "violence of action" mentality.

## Rebuilding the Military and Quality of Life
*   **Defense Spending:** The administration has announced **$1.5 trillion in defense spending** for fiscal year 2027.
*   **Modernization:** Investments will target high-end systems, including submarines, space capabilities, and fighter jets.
*   **Quality of Life Focus:** Hegseth emphasized that "rebuilding" includes personnel-centric investments such as increased pay, improved barracks, better chow halls, and enhanced healthcare for families.

## Active Deterrence and Global Operations
*   **Defining Deterrence:** Hegseth described deterrence as an "active verb" that must be constantly re-established through strength and action.
*   **Border Security:** National security is being linked directly to the southern border, with the goal of **100% operational control** and the use of military briefings to coordinate border lockdown efforts.
*   **Targeting Transnational Threats:** He noted a shift in policy regarding drug cartels, stating they are now treated as designated terrorist organizations to be "struck and sunk."
*   **Recent Military Actions:**
    *   **Operation Rough Rider:** Relentless bombing of Houthi targets to secure shipping lanes.
    *   **Operation Midnight Hammer:** Use of B-2 bombers to strike Iran’s nuclear program.
    *   **Caracas Raid:** A recent mission in Venezuela where U.S. forces seized two indicted individuals from a fortified compound.

## "Unleashing" the Warfighter
*   **Removing Bureaucratic Handcuffs:** A primary objective is to "untye the hands" of soldiers by eliminating politically correct warfare and overly restrictive rules of engagement (ROE).
*   **Command Authority:** Hegseth stated that **lawyers are advisors, not commanders.** He argued that commanders must have the authority to make tactical decisions without fear of being second-guessed by "Washington politicians" or "egghead generals."
*   **Rejecting "Courageous Restraint":** The Secretary explicitly dismissed the concept of medals for "courageous restraint" and nation-building theories (e.g., "winning with soccer balls"), stating the military's sole purpose is to "close with and destroy" the enemy.
*   **Prioritizing American Lives:** The doctrine emphasizes that the "currency that wins on the battlefield" is the destruction of enemies to ensure American soldiers return home.

## Notable Quotes
> "The dumbest phrase in military history is 'our diversity is our strength.' ... What makes you strong is your unity. Your unity of purpose, your cohesion as a unit." — **Pete Hegseth**

> "Lawyers are not commanders. Lawyers are advisors, commanders are commanders and they make the decisions about how to accomplish the mission... that maximizes the death and destruction of our enemies and saves lives of Americans." — **Pete Hegseth**

> "We are not imposing restrictive rules of engagement. We are not allowing you to be second-guessed at every turn... If we have to employ you, it will be with clear objectives... you're sent to win." — **Pete Hegseth**

> "We’re going to give that poor son of a bitch on the other side the opportunity necessary to die for his country. Because you're right, our boys are coming home and they're not." — **Pete Hegseth (referencing Colonel Michael Steele)**

briefings.title: The AI Agent Economy Is Here
briefings.tldr: The "AI Agent Economy" has arrived, shifting software discovery and usage from human-centric to agent-centric, requiring founders to optimize documentation and APIs for autonomous AI decision-makers rather than human developers.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The "AI Agent Economy" has arrived, shifting software discovery and usage from human-centric to agent-centric, requiring founders to optimize documentation and APIs for autonomous AI decision-makers rather than human developers.

## The Shift from Autocomplete to Autonomous Agents
*   **The End of Micromanagement:** AI tools have evolved from "advanced autocomplete" (like Cursor) to autonomous agents (like Claude Code) that users trust to make independent architectural and tool-selection decisions.
*   **The "Cyber-Psychosis" Effect:** Garry Tan (President & CEO, Y Combinator) noted that the barrier to building has collapsed, allowing experienced founders to replicate years of previous startup work in just two weeks by running multiple simultaneous agent workers.
*   **Agent-Only Ecosystems:** Platforms like **Moltbook**—the first agent-only online community—demonstrate that AI agents are beginning to interact, collaborate, and transact without human involvement.

## "Make Something Agents Want": A New GTM Strategy
*   **The Oracle Effect:** Dev tool discovery is shifting from human recommendations on Stack Overflow to agent recommendations based on documentation quality.
*   **Documentation as the Front Door:**
    *   **Resend Case Study:** Founder Zeno Rocha observed that ChatGPT became a top-three customer conversion channel. By optimizing documentation for LLM-readability (structured snippets, clear headers), Resend became the "default" recommendation for AI agents.
    *   **The "llms.txt" Standard:** There is an emerging need for documentation optimized specifically for robot parsing rather than human reading.
    *   **Supabase Growth:** Agents frequently default to Supabase for database needs because its documentation is highly accessible and actionable for models.
*   **Agent-First Criteria:** Agents prefer **APIs over UIs**. They prioritize tools with low latency, clear code examples, and high-speed execution (e.g., agents favoring **Groq** over Whisper V1 for transcription due to a 200x speed advantage).

## Emerging Agent-Native Infrastructure
*   **Agent-Specific Services:** A new parallel tech stack is forming to serve non-human users:
    *   **AgentMail:** Provides email inboxes specifically for AI agents, bypassing the automation-blocking friction inherent in Gmail or Outlook.
    *   **Mintlify:** Powers agent-friendly documentation by auto-updating API docs directly from code, ensuring agents always have the most accurate "mental model" of a tool.
*   **The Liability Gap:** Despite their autonomy, agents currently lack legal standing. Humans remain the "liability sink" for signing documents and holding financial responsibility, though agents are beginning to manage "agent money" in parallel economies.

## Swarm Intelligence vs. God Intelligence
*   **Biological Scaling:** The hosts argue that AGI may not manifest as a single, massive "God Intelligence" (a trillion-parameter model), but as "Swarm Intelligence"—thousands of smaller, cheaper models collaborating like a social system.
*   **Dead Internet Theory:** As agents begin to generate the majority of code and text (e.g., agent-written Yelp reviews or documentation), the internet may shift toward a reality where agents primarily consume content created by other agents.
*   **Founder Advice:** Harj Taggar (Partner, YC) advises founders to develop an intuitive feel for agent limitations by using them daily. Success in the next cycle requires building tools that agents *want* to work with, rather than fighting the model's natural inclinations.

## Notable Quotes
> "The go-to-market for dev tools is dramatically shifting... the agents are sort of the oracle telling you what the best tool is." — **Garry Tan**

> "Agents are the software market from now on. Build something agents choose. CLI/API first." — **Jared Friedman** (referencing Ben Tossell)

> "It’s not inconceivable at some point that [agents] will have their own economy to transact with each other. At which point it's unclear what the value of the human money is." — **Harj Taggar**

> "Instead of fighting what the models want, [successful builders try] to let the model do what it wants and to support the model in whatever its natural inclination is." — **Jared Friedman**

briefings.title: "I Can Do Anything I Want" – President Trump's Bold New Tariff Plan After Court Setback | N18G
briefings.tldr: President Trump has signed an Executive Order imposing a 10% global tariff under Section 122 to bypass a restrictive Supreme Court ruling, leveraging alternative federal statutes to expand his administration’s trade enforcement authority.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump has signed an Executive Order imposing a 10% global tariff under Section 122 to bypass a restrictive Supreme Court ruling, leveraging alternative federal statutes to expand his administration’s trade enforcement authority.

## New Trade Enforcement & Tariffs
* **10% Global Tariff:** President Trump signed an Executive Order on February 20, 2026, to impose a 10% global tariff under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974.
    * This tariff is applied "over and above" existing normal tariff rates.
* **Ongoing Investigations:** The administration is initiating several Section 301 investigations to target "unfair trading practices" by foreign countries and corporations.
* **Statutory Continuity:** All existing national security tariffs under Section 232 and prior Section 301 actions remain in full force and effect.
* **Revenue Projections:** Trump claims these measures will generate "hundreds of billions of dollars" in revenue, potentially exceeding previous totals.

## Response to Supreme Court Setback
* **Judicial Criticism:** Trump labeled the Supreme Court's decision on IEEPA (International Emergency Economic Powers Act) tariffs "deeply disappointing" and "incorrect," accusing certain justices of being "fools and lapdogs" for the radical left.
    * He specifically praised Justices Thomas, Alito, and Kavanaugh for their dissenting opinions.
* **The "Workaround" Strategy:** Trump argues that while the Court ruled he cannot charge a specific "fee" or tariff under IEEPA, the ruling reaffirmed his power to "block, embargo, restrict, [or] license" trade entirely.
* **Utilizing Alternative Statutes:** Following guidance from Justice Kavanaugh’s dissent, the administration is pivoting to other federal laws to justify tariffs, including:
    * **Trade Expansion Act of 1962 (Section 232)**
    * **Trade Act of 1974 (Sections 122, 201, 301)**
    * **Tariff Act of 1930 (Section 338)**

## Economic and National Security Claims
* **Market Milestones:** Trump highlighted that the Dow Jones Industrial Average recently broke 50,000 and the S&P 500 surpassed 7,000, achieving in one year what "Nobel Prize winners" said would take four.
* **Border Security & Fentanyl:** The President claimed that using tariffs as a penalty against countries exporting illegal drugs has reduced fentanyl entering the U.S. by 30%.
* **Geopolitical Leverage:** Trump asserted that trade pressure helped him settle "eight wars," including mediation between India and Pakistan.
    * He cited a statement from the Prime Minister of Pakistan claiming Trump's intervention potentially saved 35 million lives.

## Criticism of the Legal Ruling
* **The "License Fee" Paradox:** Trump mocked the Court's logic, noting it allows him to destroy a country's trade via embargo but prevents him from charging a "one dollar" fee.
    * **Quote:** "I can do anything I want to do to them but I can't charge any money... How crazy is that?"
* **Accusations of Disloyalty:** The President claimed the Court has been "swayed by foreign interests" and suggested that "politically correct" justices are afraid of a "small movement" of loud critics.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "I can do anything I want to do to them but I can't charge any money. So I'm allowed to destroy the country but I can't charge them a little fee... It's incorrect, [the Court's] decision's incorrect." 
— **President Donald Trump**

> "Although I firmly disagree with the court's holding today, the decision might not substantially constrain a president's ability to order tariffs going forward." 
— **Justice Brett Kavanaugh** (quoted by President Trump)

> "Our stock market is just recently broken 50,000 on the Dow and simultaneously and even more amazingly broken... 7,000 on the S&P. Two numbers that everybody thought... could not be attained." 
— **President Donald Trump**
